required_runtime_proof: host creates at least two independent Lua VM states and can destroy one without corrupting the other
host catches a script error and performs deterministic cleanup without losing host control
Lua state is explicitly released on normal completion and error completion
OS, IO, and native-module access are unavailable unless individually allow-listed by the host
only required host functions are exposed to Lua
host retains the main execution loop and performance-critical/resource-critical work
runtime type checks enforce documented host/Lua boundary types
JIT remains optional; any future deoptimization path preserves reconstructible execution state
generated or contributed Lua remains readable enough for human audit without hidden magic
proof_ceiling: Harness readiness and static contract proof only. No Lua interpreter, host adapter, sandbox runtime, bytecode execution, JIT behavior, memory isolation, or live host/Lua behavior is implemented or proven by this contract.
